component.name: KAthenaeum
component.summary: Offline Wikipedia library with a local AI research assistant

description.p: KAthenaeum turns Kiwix ZIM files into a searchable library on your own computer. Ask a question and get an answer written by a small local language model, with every sentence linked back to the Wikipedia article it came from.
Nothing leaves your machine: no cloud service, no account, no tracking.

Tools for studying: highlight passages in four colours and write notes on them, gathered on a Notes page; cite any article in MLA, APA or Chicago style, with a bibliography for each project and works cited added to exported documents; look up a word in an installed Wiktionary from the right-click menu; and show the place an article is about on your maps.

A handbook in KDE's Help Center. A more current look: a sidebar with search, page titles in the header, cards, compact buttons and segmented tabs. Map regions chosen by their shapes, the map reopening where it was left, articles across the whole window, and a check for newer versions of your libraries.
Research projects: have the AI write a report to your own instructions, planned in sections, each written from the sources that fit it, with citations and a reference list added by KAthenaeum.
Offline maps: download the world overview and the regions you choose in Settings, browse them without a connection, and click a place to open its Wikipedia article from your libraries.
Project documents open in a window of their own with Kate's editor: Markdown highlighting, spell check, search and replace, vi mode, beside a live preview.

A full review: the interface can no longer reach the network except the Kiwix catalog, oversized or hostile library files are refused, removing a library while searching no longer crashes, answers and drafts keep going when you leave their page, and many smaller fixes. A new icon.
Projects: AI-drafted summaries and chat notes, saved passages highlighted in their articles, and your notes shown in a document's preview.
Research projects: collect articles, saved passages, answers and chats with notes; ask questions answered from the project; write Markdown documents that cite its sources, and export them.
Ask about this article: a chat panel beside every article that answers from that article alone, with citations to its sections. Ask about selected text.
Ask: answers from your libraries written by a local model, with every sentence linked to its source and unsupported sentences flagged. Follow-up questions, saved chats, and model settings.
Search: titles as you type, then the text of every article in every library, with the matching passage shown.
Library Manager: browse the Kiwix catalog, download and verify libraries, manage installed ones. Reading: library home, A to Z, and articles with their pictures.
